description: Heatwave days that people were exposed to on average each year, 2020–2024, in the world and in each of 220 countries and territories: as observed, as expected in a modelled climate without human-caused warming, and the difference attributable to climate change, from the Lancet Countdown (indicator 1.1.1). Estimates for small countries are more uncertain, as the producer notes; where a country had fewer heatwave days than its modelled counterfactual, the attributable value is negative.

processing.description: Read the sheets '2025_Report _Data_Global' (the world) and '2025_Report_Data_Country' (220 countries and territories by ISO3 code) of the indicator 1.1.1 (attributable heatwave days) workbook of the Lancet Countdown 2025 report, 2020–2024: heatwave days observed, expected without climate change (Counterfactual) and attributable to climate change (Attributable_to_CC), published as in the workbook. The producer's country names, WHO regions and HDI levels are not published.
Mapped each ISO3 code to the site's entity of that code (pipeline/geo/entities.csv); every code is in it.

Checked that observed days equal expected days plus attributable days in every row, and that every country has a value for each year of the world sheet. A country with fewer heatwave days than its modelled counterfactual has a negative attributable value, published as it is.

scope.basis: A heatwave is at least two consecutive days when both minimum and maximum temperature exceed the local 1986–2005 95th percentile. Observed days from ERA5; days expected without human-caused warming from 24 paired CMIP6 climate model simulations. Each country's value is its people's average.
scope.geography: World, and countries and territories as the producer draws them (UN territories)

title: Heatwave days per person, observed and attributable to climate change, world and by country
